chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Ja'far Al-Sa'igh, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abu Hanifa was with him. So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I saw a strange dream.' He said to me, 'O Ibn Muslim, bring it forth, for the one knowledgeable about it is seated here,' and he gestured with his hand to Abu Hanifa. I said, 'I saw as if I had entered my house, and my family had come out at me, breaking many walnuts and scattering them upon me. So I was astonished by this dream.' Abu Hanifa said, 'You are a man who disputes and argues bitterly regarding the inheritance of your family, so after great hardship you will attain your need from it, if Allah wills.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'You have hit it, by Allah, O Abu Hanifa.'

He said, 'Then Abu Hanifa left from his presence, so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I disliked the interpretation of this Hostile One (Nasibi).' He said, 'O Ibn Muslim, may Allah not displease you. Their interpretation does not match our interpretation, nor does our interpretation match theirs, and the interpretation is not as he has interpreted it.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you said 'you hit it' and swore upon it, while he was mistaken.' He said, 'Yes, I swore that he hit the mistake.'

I said to him, 'So what is its interpretation?' He said, 'O Ibn Muslim, you will do Mut'ah with a woman, and your family will learn of it, so she will tear up new clothes for you, for the shell is the clothing of the nut.'

Ibn Muslim said, 'By Allah, there was not a Friday between his interpretation and the verification of the dream. So when it was the morning of the Friday, I was sitting at the door when a maid passed by me who pleased me. So I ordered my slave to bring her back, then I brought her into my house and I enjoyed her. My family sensed it and they came into the house. The maid hastened towards the door and I remained, so she tore up new clothes for me which I used to wear during the Eids.'

And Musa Al-Zawwar the perfumer came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, I saw a dream that alarmed me. I saw my brother-in-law who was dead embracing me, and I feared that the term (of death) had drawn near.' He said, 'O Musa, expect death morning and evening, for it will meet us. And the embracing of the dead by the living is longevity for their lives.' He said, 'What is the name of your brother-in-law?' He said, 'Husayn.' He said, 'Indeed, your dream indicates your remaining alive and your visiting Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), for everyone who is embraced by one named Husayn will visit him, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: The Hostile One (referring to Abu Hanifa in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of seeing a dead person named Husayn embracing you in a dream according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the distinct epistemological authority of the Imams in dream interpretation, contrasting Imam Al-Sadiq’s precise insight with the scholarly intuition of Abu Hanifa, who was deemed a 'Nasibi' (rival) yet accurate in his specific case. The narrative underscores the Shia view that while non-Shia scholars may occasionally hit the mark, their interpretive framework differs fundamentally from the Ahl al-Bayt, as illustrated by the correction regarding the tearing of clothes and the symbolic meaning of embracing a namesake of Husayn.

en.hubeali: H 14895 – Ali, from his father, from Al-Hassan Bin Ali from Abu Ja’far Al-Sa’ig, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said:

‘I came up to Abu Abdullahasws and in hisasws presence was Abu Hanifa. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws, I saw a strange dream’. So heasws said to me: ‘O Ibn Muslim, relate it for the knowledgeable one for he is seated here’ – and heasws indicated by hisasws hand to Abu Hanifa. So I said, ‘I saw as if I had entered my house, and my wife came out at me. She broke many walnuts and scattered them upon me. So I was astounded by this dream’. So Abu Hanifala said, ‘You are a man who disputed and argued regarding the inheritance of your wife, and after your share of difficulties you will achieve your needs from her, Allahazwj Willing’.  Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘By Allahazwj, O Abu Hanifala, you’ve hit it’.

(The narrator) said, ‘Then Abu Hanifa<sup>la</sup> went out from his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, I do not like the interpretation of this Hostile One (Nasibi)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Ibn Muslim, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will not Displease you. Their interpretation does not coincide with our<sup>asws</sup> interpretation, nor does our<sup>asws</sup> interpretation coincide with theirs, and the interpretation (of your dream) is not as he has interpreted it’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, you<sup>asws</sup> said that he hit it, and swore upon it, whilst he was mistaken’. He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘Yes, I<sup>asws</sup> did swear that he hit the mistake’.

So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So what is its interpretation?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Ibn Muslim, you will do Muttah with a woman and your wife would come to know of it. So she would tear up your new clothes, for the walnut shells are the clothing for the nuts’.

Ibn Muslim said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, there was not a Friday between his<sup>asws</sup> interpretation and the verification of the dream. So when it was the morning of the Friday, I was seated at the door when a maid passed by who caught my eye. So I sent my slave to return her. Then I entered her into my house. I did Muttah with her. My wife sensed it and she came up to us in the house. The maid took the initiative and went to the door, and I remained. So she tore up my new clothes which I had worn during the Eid’.

And Musa Al-Zawwaar the perfume seller went to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I saw a dream which shocked me. I saw my dead brother-in-law embrace me, and I am scared that my term (death) is near’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Musa! You should expect death morning and evening for it will meet us. And the embracing by the dead to the living is longevity of life for them. So what is the name of your brother in law?’ he said, ‘Husayn’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But your dream is evidence of your remaining (alive), and your visiting Abu Abdullah (Al-Husayn)<sup>asws</sup>, for everyone who is embraced by someone who is named Al-Husayn would visit him<sup>asws</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
en.sarwar: 448. Ismail Bin Abdullah Al-Qarshy who said:

A man came up to Abu Abdullah (a.s.), so he said to him (a.s.), ‘O son (a.s.) of the Messenger (a.s.) of Allah (azwj), I saw in my dream as if I was outside of the city of Al-Kufa in a place which I recognised, and there was a ghost of a man made of wood, riding a wooden horse and waving his sword, and I saw him and was terrified and in a panic’. So he (a.s.) said to him: ‘You are a man who wants to assassinate a man for his livelihood, so fear Allah (azwj) Who Created you, then will Cause you to die’.

So the man said, ‘I testify that you (a.s.) have received Knowledge and have extracted it from its mine. I inform you (a.s.), O son (a.s.) of the Rasool Allah (saww) that you (a.s.) have interpreted (correctly) for me. There was a man in my neighbourhood who came to me and presented to me his asset, so I thought that I should own it for much less as I realised that there is no other seeker for it apart from me’.
So Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said: ‘And your companion has befriended us (a.s.) rather our (a.s.) enemies?’

He said, ‘Yes, O son (a.s.) of the Rasool Allah (saww), a good man with foresight, resolute in the Religion, and I repent to Allah (azwj) and to you (a.s.) from what I was thinking of and intended for. So, inform me, O son (a.s.) of the Rasool Allah (saww), had he been a Hostile One (Nasibi), would it have been permissible for me to assassinate him?’
He (a.s.) said: ‘Fulfil the trust to the one who has entrusted you and wants advice from you even if it is to the killer of Al-Husayn (a.s.)’.
